chunks: If a man dies and leaves behind a wife and a brother—whether the brother is from the father alone, from both the father and mother, or from the mother alone—the wife receives one-fourth, and what remains goes to the brother. Likewise, if he leaves behind a wife and a sister—whether from the father alone, from both the father and mother, or from the mother alone—the wife receives one-fourth, and what remains goes to the sister.

If he leaves behind a wife, a maternal brother, a full brother, and a paternal brother, the wife receives one-fourth, the maternal brother receives one-sixth, and what remains goes to the full brother, while the paternal brother is excluded.

If he leaves behind a wife, a maternal brother and sister, or maternal brothers and sisters, and full brothers and sisters, and paternal brothers and sisters, then the wife receives one-fourth, the maternal siblings receive one-third, with male and female equal in that share, and what remains goes to the full siblings, with the male receiving the share of two females. The paternal siblings are excluded.

If a woman dies and leaves behind her husband and a brother—whether from the father, the mother, or both—then the husband receives one-half, and what remains goes to the brother. Likewise, if she leaves behind her husband and her sister—whether from the father, the mother, or both—then the husband receives one-half, and what remains goes to the sister.

If she leaves behind her husband, maternal brothers and sisters, full brothers and sisters, and paternal brothers and sisters, then the husband receives one-half, the maternal siblings receive one-third divided equally among them, and what remains—namely one-sixth—goes to the full siblings, with the male receiving the share of two females. The paternal siblings are excluded.

If she leaves behind her husband, a maternal brother, a full brother, and a paternal brother, then the husband receives one-half, the maternal brother receives one-sixth, and what remains goes to the full brother, while the paternal brother is excluded. Likewise, the shares of the children of brothers and sisters, together with the husband and wife, proceed according to this rule.

key_terms.سَقَطَ الْأَخُ مِنَ الْأَبِ: The paternal brother is excluded from inheriting.
key_terms.سِهَامُ وُلْدِ الْإِخْوَةِ وَالْأَخَوَات: The inheritance shares of the children of brothers and sisters.
key_terms.لِلذَّكَرِ مِثْلُ حَظِّ الْأُنْثَيَيْنِ: The male receives a share equal to that of two females.

ai.seo_question: How is inheritance divided between a spouse and brothers or sisters in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith sets out inheritance rulings for a husband or wife when the remaining heirs are brothers and sisters of different categories: maternal, paternal, and full siblings. It explains the fixed shares, the equal division among maternal siblings, the rule that full siblings take precedence over paternal siblings, and that the same pattern applies to the children of siblings.
